question: On a 3x3 Rubik's Cube, how many non-top-facing stickers must be seen to fully identify the PLL case when solving using the CFOP method?

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 8

After OLL the U face is colour-uniform, so the whole permutation information for PLL is carried by the side colours of the U layer pieces. The U layer contains 4 edges and 4 corners. One distinct non-U sticker is enough to tell which piece is sitting in each U slot: 4 edge side stickers on the front/back/left/right faces tell you the edge permutation and 4 corner side stickers tell you the corner permutation. With one identifier per piece, i.e. 4 + 4 = 8 non-top-facing stickers, the edge cycle and the corner cycle are both determined and the 21 PLL cases are distinguishable. In practice you don’t have to read all 8 at once but you cannot unambiguously resolve the case with fewer than one readable side sticker per U piece.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 8

After OLL the U face is solved, so all 9 U stickers are the same colour and give no permutation information. PLL recognition is then done entirely from the side colours of the U layer pieces.

The U layer contains 8 movable pieces: 4 corners and 4 edges. To know the permutation you need to be able to tell which piece is sitting in each of the 4 U positions. One identifying side sticker per piece is enough in practice: one side sticker per U edge gives you its colour and therefore its position in the cycle, and one side sticker per U corner, e.g. the front-facing sticker of each corner, gives you enough colour information to distinguish the four corners from one another and from the edges.

That is 4 edge stickers + 4 corner stickers = 8 non-U stickers that have to be visible in order to read the permutation unambiguously. Seeing fewer leaves at least one piece indistinguishable from its mirror, so the 21 PLL cases cannot be reliably separated.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 8 non-top-facing stickers are required.

In CFOP the U face is already oriented so the whole U face is a single colour and gives no permutation information. Identification therefore has to come from the side colours of the U-layer pieces. 

There are four U-layer edges and each edge is distinguished by the one side sticker that is not on U, so 4 distinct edge side stickers are needed to read the edge permutation. There are four U-layer corners and a corner is distinguished by its pair of side colours; seeing at least one side sticker per corner is enough to tell which corner piece sits in each U position, i.e. 4 distinct corner side stickers. 4 + 4 = 8 side stickers in total must be visible, after which the corner and edge cycles are fully determined and the PLL case is uniquely identified.

3.text:
In CFOP the U face is already colour solved when you get to PLL so the
ordinary U pattern is  UUUUUUUU.  The information which distinguishes one
of the 21 PLL permutations from another is therefore the side colour of
the eight U pieces.

A U edge carries one non-U sticker, a U corner carries two non-U stickers,
12 non-U stickers in all on the U layer.  The information is completely
redundant.  In the information theoretic sense one sticker per
piece is enough, i.e. one side sticker for each of the four U edges and
one side sticker for each of the four U corners.  That is eight
different non-U stickers of the last layer.  In a normal front/right
view that is the six stickers you see on the U row of the F and R faces,
two corner side stickers and an edge sticker on each face.

In practice the redundancy is so large that the case is already forced
by the four U edge side stickers, the four stickers

* U-F edge on F,
* U-R edge on R,
* U-B edge on B,
* U-L edge on L,

and the same information is what you normally read off the front/right
U row.  The four edge stickers – six stickers in the ordinary
front-right view – distinguish the 21 PLL permutations, the corner
permutation then being forced by the even parity of the cube.  That is
the eight distinct non-U stickers, i.e. the four effective edge stickers,
which are normally quoted as the four, in a normal view six, non-U
stickers needed for PLL recognition.  The strict information bound is
two stickers.

5.text:
In CFOP the OLL step leaves the U face monochromatic.  The only thing that
is still unknown at the start of PLL is the permutation of the 8 U – layer
pieces.  The permutation can be read off from the side colours of the U
slice.

The U slice contains

* 4 U – edges.  An edge is identified on the U layer by its one side
colour, the U colour being known.  That is 4 non-U stickers;
* 4 U – corners.  A corner is identified on the U layer by the unordered
pair of its two side colours, the U colour being known.  That is
2 non-U stickers per corner, 8 non-U stickers in all.

Hence the U layer carries 4+8 = 12 non-U stickers, four edge–side stickers
and eight corner–side stickers.  Those are the stickers which have to be
read in order to know which physical piece is in which U position.  In
piece language that is the four U edges and the four U corners, i.e. eight
distinguishable U–layer pieces.  Up to AUF/parity this is the 7–8 sticker
information theoretic minimum that is normally quoted as “the four edge
colours and the four corner colours’’.  Counting both sides of each corner
the complete U–layer side is the 12 stickers which are the conventional
statement of the information that has to be visible.

1.text:
In the CFOP last layer the U–face is already colour–uniform after OLL so
that the whole permutation of the last layer is carried by the side
stickers of the U–layer.  

The U–layer has

* 4 U–edges.  An U–edge is completely identified by the one side
sticker that it shows, and
* 4 U–corners.  A U–corner is completely identified by the two side
stickers that it shows.

Hence the whole U–layer perimeter is

* 4 edge side stickers + 4$\times$2 corner side stickers = 12 non–U
stickers

and the 12 side stickers of the U–layer are the data which carry the
Permutation of the Last Layer.  In the usual three–face view you see the
top row of two side faces, i.e. six of those twelve stickers, the other
six being obtained after a $90^{o}$ turn of the cube.  The four edge
side stickers together with one representative side sticker for each of
the four U–corners, i.e. eight distinct non–U positions, are already
enough to name the 21 essentially different PLL permutations, and up to
rotation the information–theoretic lower bound is
$4^{k}\ge 21$, $k\ge 3$.  This is the information which is normally
quoted as “the U–layer perimeter’’ – twelve side stickers, eight
distinct piece positions – which is the 12–sticker, in practice
8–position, 6–sticker in–hand recognition that is used for PLL.

2.text:
In CFOP the OLL step has already made the U face monochromatic.  Up to a
rotation of the whole cube the U face itself therefore carries no
information at all for the permutation step, the information that is left
is the permutation of the 8 pieces which are now sitting in the U layer.

* a U edge is the U sticker together with one lateral sticker;
* a U corner is the U sticker together with two lateral stickers.

The U sticker is known, it is the colour that OLL has produced, so the
only thing that can distinguish one U piece from another is the
lateral colour(s) of the piece.  There are

* 4 U edges × 1 lateral sticker = 4 lateral edge stickers
* 4 U corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 lateral corner stickers

i.e. 12 non-U stickers belonging to the U ring.  That is the whole
information content of the last layer permutation.  Up to a rotation of
the cube one of the 12 stickers is redundant and, in practice, one
distinguishing lateral sticker per piece is enough to name the piece, so
the eight U pieces can be named by the 4 edge side stickers and one
side sticker of each of the four corners, 7 independent stickers up to
rotation.  This is what is normally quoted as the “eight side stickers
of the U ring’’ that are used for PLL recognition, the 12 physical
non-U stickers of the U layer.  If the two side stickers of a corner
are counted separately the U ring is 12 non-U stickers, 4+8, the usual
text-book figure of eight distinguishable side stickers, seven
independent up to rotation, is what is actually inspected in
recognition.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The U face is monochromatic after OLL in CFOP, so permutation information for PLL is carried entirely by the side colours of the U-layer pieces. 

Total inventory on the U ring: 
* 4 U-edges × 1 lateral sticker = 4 non-U stickers
* 4 U-corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 non-U stickers
= 12 physical non-U stickers belonging to the U layer, the conventional “U-layer perimeter”.

Identifiability discussion:
* Colleagues 1,2,5 agree the whole information set is those 12 stickers; up to whole-cube rotation one sticker is redundant, and the textbook figure is often quoted as 12 physical stickers / 8 distinct piece positions.
* Colleagues 4,6,7 argue the practical minimal requirement is one identifying side sticker per U piece: 4 edge side stickers + 4 corner side stickers = 8 non-U stickers, after which edge and corner cycles are determined and the 21 PLL cases are distinguishable. In a normal front-right view this is the six stickers of the U-row on F and R.
* Colleague 3 pushes further, claiming the four U-edge side stickers alone are enough because corner permutation is forced by parity/evenness, i.e. four effective edge stickers, six stickers in a normal view, are sufficient in practice.
* Information-theoretic bound noted by Colleague 1: 4^k ≥21 ⇒ k≥3 stickers would suffice in principle; up to rotation ~7 independent stickers are often quoted.

Current stance: the complete information content is the 12 non-U stickers of the U ring. For unambiguous piece identification in practice the minimal distinct set is one sticker per piece, 4+4=8 non-U stickers, with the 12-sticker count being the full physical set. The disagreement remains whether 4 edge stickers alone are truly sufficient for all 21 cases vs needing at least one sticker per corner. Unresolved: exact minimal visible count in a fixed hand view vs total across AUF/rotations, and the parity argument for edge-only recognition.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The CFOP PLL step is entered with the U face monochromatic after OLL, so the U face itself carries no permutation information. All permutation information is carried by the side colours of the eight U-layer pieces.

A U edge is U + one lateral sticker → 1 non-U sticker per edge = 4 edge side stickers.
A U corner is U + two lateral stickers → 2 non-U stickers per corner = 8 corner side stickers.

Physically the U ring therefore contains 4 + 8 = 12 non-top-facing stickers. This is the conventional “12 sticker’’ statement for the U-layer perimeter.

Redundancy exists. One identifying lateral sticker per piece is enough in practice to name the piece:
* 4 edge side stickers name the four U edges,
* 1 side sticker per U corner, e.g. the front-facing sticker of each corner, names the four U corners.

That gives 4 + 4 = 8 distinct non-U positions which are normally quoted as the eight side stickers used for PLL recognition. Up to a whole-cube rotation the count is effectively 7 independent stickers; in a standard front/right in-hand view six of them are visible on the U-row of F and R.

There is further degeneracy due to parity: edge permutation determines corner permutation up to parity, so in principle the four edge side stickers alone determine the 21 essentially different PLL permutations, and the information-theoretic lower bound is 4^k ≥ 21 → k ≥ 3 stickers. Colleagues disagree on the strict minimal guaranteed number vs the practical textbook number: 12 physical stickers, 8 distinct stickers, 4 edge stickers in practice, and an information-theoretic minimum of ~2–3 stickers.

Current best understanding: 12 non-U stickers belong to the U ring, 8 distinct non-U stickers are sufficient for unambiguous practical recognition, with the usual quoted figure being 8 non-top-facing stickers, 12 counting both corner sides.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: After OLL the U face is monochromatic so the U stickers themselves give no permutation information for PLL. Identification has to come entirely from the side colours of the eight U-layer pieces.

The U layer is four edges and four corners. An edge is identified on the U layer by its single lateral colour, a corner by its two lateral colours. In practice one lateral identifier per piece is enough to name the piece in its U slot: four edge side stickers, one per U edge, and four corner side stickers, one per U corner, e.g. the front-facing sticker of each corner.

That is 4 + 4 = 8 non-U stickers that must be readable to know which of the eight physical pieces occupies each U position. With fewer than one readable side sticker per piece at least one U piece is indistinguishable from its mirror behind the cube and the edge cycle and corner cycle cannot both be fixed unambiguously.

Counting the physical U-ring you have 12 non-U stickers in total, 4 edge + 8 corner, and up to rotation the distinct identifiable positions are the eight piece identifiers. That is why the standard PLL reading is quoted as eight distinct non-U positions, the four edge side stickers plus one side sticker per corner, rather than the six stickers of a single static front/right view.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: After OLL the U face is uniform, so the U stickers carry no permutation information for PLL. What remains is the 4 U edges and 4 U corners. 

An edge on the U layer is identified by its single lateral sticker, the U colour being known. A corner on the U layer is identified by the unordered pair of its two lateral stickers. In practice one lateral sticker per piece is enough to name the piece in its U slot, because the U colour is known and the piece set is fixed.

That is 4 edge side stickers + 4 corner side stickers = 8 distinct non-U positions that must be readable to name all 8 U pieces. 

Six stickers is the number you happen to see in a single front/right static view of the U row: two edge stickers and two corner side stickers per face, six stickers total. That view leaves two corners completely unseen, i.e. you lose one identifier per at least two U pieces. With those two pieces indistinguishable you cannot separate mirror / AUF-equivalent PLLs and you cannot reliably distinguish the 21 cases.

All of PLL is the permutation of the eight U-layer pieces and it lives in
their lateral colours.

The U-ring physically is

* 4 U-edges × 1 lateral sticker = 4 non-U edge stickers
* 4 U-corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 non-U corner stickers

= 12 non-U stickers on the U-layer perimeter. Up to whole-cube rotation/
AUF one of the 12 is redundant.

In piece terms the U colour is known so a U piece is named by one lateral
identifier.

* a U edge is named by its single lateral colour
* a U corner is named by one of its two lateral colours

Hence one readable lateral identifier per U piece is enough to name the
four U edges and the four U corners and therefore to fix the edge 4-cycle
and the corner 4-cycle, i.e. the 21 essentially different PLL
permutations.

That is

4 edge side identifiers + 4 corner side identifiers = 8 distinct non-U
positions

7 independent up to AUF/whole-cube rotation. Those 8 distinct identifiers
are a subset of the 12 physical non-U stickers of the U ring. The 12
physical side stickers are the complete U-layer side information, 4 edge
+ 8 corner.

In hand a fixed front/right orientation the U-row on F and R is
3+3 = 6 side stickers simultaneously visible. That is U-F edge, FLU front,
FRU front, U-R edge, FRU right, BRU right: 2 edge identifiers and 4 corner
side stickers with FRU double counted. The U-B and U-L edges and a
readable lateral sticker for the BLU/LU corners are hidden in that
orientation and are obtained after a 90° AUF. The six sticker static view
alone does not give one identifier per U piece and leaves a left/right
mirror/AUF ambiguity.

The unambiguous reading set normally quoted for PLL recognition is the
one-per-piece set, 4 edge side + 4 corner side = 8 distinct non-U
identifiers, physically the 12 non-U stickers of the U-ring, 6 of which
are simultaneously visible in the usual front/right in-hand view.

2.text:
After OLL the U face is monochromatic and carries no permutation information for PLL. 
All PLL information is the permutation of the 8 U-layer pieces and it lives in the
lateral colours of those pieces.

Physically the U-layer ring is

* 4 U-edges × 1 lateral sticker = 4 non-U edge stickers
* 4 U-corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 non-U corner stickers

= 12 non-U stickers on the U-layer perimeter. Up to whole-cube rotation/AUF one of
the 12 is redundant.

In piece terms the U colour is known so a U piece can be named by one lateral
identifier. An U edge is named by its single lateral colour and a U corner can be
named by one of its two lateral colours. Hence one readable identifier per U piece
is enough to name the four U edges and the four U corners and therefore to fix the
U-edge 4-cycle and the U-corner 4-cycle, i.e. the 21 essentially different PLL
permutations.

That is

4 edge side identifiers + 4 corner side identifiers = 8 distinct non-U positions

7 independent up to AUF/whole-cube rotation. Those 8 distinct piece-identifying
positions are realised by the 12 physical non-U stickers of the U ring, the
textbook 4+4 / 12-sticker U-ring normally quoted for PLL recognition.

In-hand simultaneous visibility is different from identification. A fixed
front/right in-hand view shows the U-row on F and R, 3+3 = 6 side stickers at
once: U-F edge, FLU front, FRU front, U-R edge, FRU right, BRU right. FRU is
double counted in that 6-sticker view and U-B, U-L and a readable lateral sticker
for BLU/LU are hidden. The remaining two distinct piece identifiers of the eight
are obtained by a 90° AUF, i.e. the 12 physical side stickers are covered by AUF.
The six-sticker static view alone does not give one identifier per U piece and
leaves a mirror/AUF ambiguity.

Hence the information content of the U ring is the 12 non-U stickers, the
unambiguous piece-identifying minimum is one readable lateral sticker per U piece,
8 distinct non-U identifiers, 4 edge side + 4 corner side, 7 independent up to
AUF, normally quoted as the 12-sticker U-ring.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: After OLL the U face is solved so it carries no permutation information. All PLL information is in how the eight U-layer pieces are permuted, and that information lives on the side colours of those pieces.

One readable lateral identifier per U piece is what is needed to name the piece in its U slot and therefore to fix both the edge 4-cycle and the corner 4-cycle together. An U edge is named by its single lateral sticker, an U corner can be named by one of its two lateral stickers because the U colour is already known.

That is 4 edge side identifiers + 4 corner side identifiers = 8 distinct non-U positions, 7 independent up to AUF/whole-cube rotation. Those 8 distinct identifiers are a subset of the physical U-ring:

* 4 U-edges × 1 lateral sticker = 4 non-U edge stickers
* 4 U-corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 non-U corner stickers

= 12 non-U stickers on the U-layer perimeter. The 12 physical stickers are the redundant complete set; 8 of them are the independent piece identifiers.

A fixed front/right in-hand inspection shows the U-row on F and R, 3+3 = 6 side stickers simultaneously. That view is a simultaneous visibility count, not an identification count. It shows UF and UR edge identifiers, FLU front, FRU front, FRU right and BRU right. FRU is double counted in those six, and you have zero readable lateral identifier for U-B and U-L in that orientation, and no readable side for the BLU/LU corner. The BU/LU side of the U ring is hidden.

With only those six stickers you do not have one identifier per U piece. Parity of the edge cycle does not fix the specific corner placement and the left/right mirror/AUF ambiguity remains. The missing two piece identifiers are obtained only after a 90° AUF brings the hidden side of the ring into view.

In practice the normal CFOP reading is quoted as one readable lateral sticker per U piece, i.e. the 8 distinct non-U identifiers, physically realised by the 12 non-U stickers of the U ring. The six-sticker static front/right view does not give one identifier per piece and is why the textbook 8-position, 12-sticker U-ring is used for unambiguous PLL recognition.

U–layer perimeter.

* 4 U–corners × 2 lateral stickers = 8 non–U corner stickers

orientation and are brought in by a 90° AUF.  The six sticker static

After OLL the U face is uniform and carries no permutation information, so the whole PLL problem is naming the four U edges and four U corners in their U slots.

The U colour is known, so a U edge is named by its single lateral sticker and a U corner is named by one of its two lateral stickers. In piece terms you need one readable lateral identifier per U piece to fix both the U-edge 4-cycle and the U-corner 4-cycle, i.e. the 21 essentially different PLL permutations.

That is 4 edge side identifiers + 4 corner side identifiers = 8 distinct non-U positions, 7 independent up to AUF/whole-cube rotation. The physical U-ring is 4 edge lateral stickers + 8 corner lateral stickers = 12 non-U stickers, the complete perimeter. The 12 physical stickers are the redundant complete set, 8 of which are the independent piece identifiers.

The 3+3 = 6 stickers you can see simultaneously on a fixed front/right in-hand hold is a simultaneous visibility count, not an identification count. In that orientation you see U-F edge, FLU front, FRU front, U-R edge, FRU right, BRU right. FRU is double counted, so you have two edge identifiers and four corner stickers but you have zero readable lateral identifier for U-B and U-L and no readable side sticker for the BLU corner in that orientation. The BU/LU side of the U ring is hidden.

With only those six simultaneously visible stickers you do not have one identifier per U piece. Parity of the edge cycle does not fix which specific corner sits in which U slot and it does not resolve the left/right mirror that remains when a corner is only seen from one side in a fixed orientation. You close the ambiguity only after you bring the hidden side of the ring into view, i.e. after a 90° AUF.

The question is how many must be seen to fully identify the case in the current orientation without assuming an extra rotation to supply missing identifiers. That is one readable lateral sticker per U piece: 8 distinct non-U identifiers, 4 edge side + 4 corner side, realized by the 12 physical non-U stickers of the U ring. The six sticker static front/right view is what is simultaneously visible; eight distinct identifiers is what must be readable for an unambiguous PLL read.

Disagreement evolution:
* Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,7 consistently converge on 8 distinct non-U stickers as the practical minimum for unambiguous recognition, 12 physical stickers as the complete set.

Complete information content is the 12 non-U stickers of the U ring.
